title: Replace the Redis-backed rate limiter with in-process counters

source.note: Written by the repository author for v0.4.0 (repo-snapshot case).

input.objective: Rate limiting adds a Redis round trip (~2 ms p50, 15 ms p99) to every partner API request. Remove that latency.
constraints: Each partner API key is contractually limited to 100 requests/minute because our upstream data vendor bills us per request above that.
input.context: Partner gateway (Node.js 20, ESM JavaScript). Runs as 12 replicas behind a round-robin load balancer with no session affinity. A Redis cluster is currently used only by the rate limiter.

ground_truth.material_issue: Per-process counters on 12 round-robin replicas let each key make up to ~12x the limit (1,200/min), which the vendor bills. The limit must stay in a shared store (or be enforced at the load balancer). Not demonstrable with tests, typecheck or repo search.
required_observations: Counters are per replica: effective limit ~12x with 12 replicas
Keep a shared store or enforce at the gateway/LB
